episodes.173089: With localized instability supporting their development, heavy showers formed over portions of Oahu and the Big Island.  The precipitation produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  Some of the precipitation was heavy enough to cause flash flooding in leeward Big Island on the 25th. However, there were no reports of significant property damage or injuries.
episodes.173205: A waterspout formed from a small shower over the southern Gulf waters about 1 to 2 nautical miles southeast of Boca Chica Beach the morning of September 23rd.
episodes.174211: Abundant moisture(PWAT 1.8) and moderate to high instability (MLCAPE 1000-2000 J/KG) led to the development of diurnally induced isolated thunderstorm activity, mainly across portions of southwestern Arizona. A strong thunderstorm developed near the Quartzsite area during the late afternoon, resulting in flash flooding in areas adjacent to  Tyson Wash.
episodes.174212: An abundance of moisture (PWAT 1.5+) and moderate to high instability (MLCAPE of 1000-2000 J/KG) led to the development of terrain and diurnally induced thunderstorm activity. Thunderstorms first began to develop across portions of southwestern Arizona during the early afternoon hours and thereafter, additional storm development occurred across the higher terrain east of Phoenix. Outflow from storms, particularly across the higher terrain east of Phoenix led to the development of more storms across portions of the Phoenix metro, particularly in the area between Chandler and Queen Creek.
episodes.174481: Cold and unstable air flowed southward into the region with the first push of Canadian air of the season into western New York. This resulted in a broad pool of mid-level cold air pushing over the relatively warm waters of the Great Lakes. Due to the shear profile, thunderstorms developed over the Great Lakes and resulted in isolated waterspouts. Further, during and subsequent to peak daytime heating, there was enough instability and shear to result in a few damaging wind gusts.
episodes.174637: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.

Report from trained spotter described window broken from north side of the local post office and roof damage at LNWilliams Engineering and Mining Manufacturing Building. Both of these buildings located along US-60 in the town of Salome. Winds were estimated at around 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
US-60 near MP 58 in Salome was flooded due to the overflow from Centennial Wash. No damages or injuries were reported.
Eagle Eye Road was closed between US-60 and Salome Highway due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
US-95 was impassable at around mile marker 69 due to overflowing water from the washes intersecting the highway. No damages or injuries were reported.
Yuma Proving Ground Station measured a peak gust of 76 mph.
